steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: No sense waiting, guapa. This weapon store is closed.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Eh?

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: You're a tourist, right? The store was pretty well known in Dossoles before. The owner always got a bunch of great wares that nobody else could ever get their hands on.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Yeah, I know.

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: But it's been a long time since it last opened for business.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I know that, too.

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: Wow, I didn't expect you to know so much about Dossoles.

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: But I'm sure there's one thing you didn't know.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: Land is very valuable here in Dossoles, and this store is in an excellent location. Normally, it would have been rented out to another tenant long ago.

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: But it's been almost a year since this store closed down, and it hasn't been rented out to everyone else.

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: Do you know why?

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: This is no mere secret. Most common folk don't know about this. If you want to know, come buy a boutique from me, and I'll let you in on it. What do you say?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Because the owner and Mayor Candela have a close relationship.

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: What, you know that too?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Of course I do.

steps.name: Tourist
steps.text: Thief! C-Catch him!

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I'll go help out.

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: Her moves are light... Just like... una pluma.

steps.name: Criminal
steps.text: Heheh, nice haul today.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Stop right there.

steps.name: Criminal
steps.text: Who are you?!

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Hand back what you stole.

steps.name: Criminal
steps.text: And here I was wondering since when the pacos have been so efficient.

steps.name: Criminal
steps.text: So it's just una chavala.

steps.name: Criminal
steps.text: Little girl, did your parents ever tell you that playing hero here in Dossoles could get you killed...?
Before the criminal could finish his sentence, La Pluma had already advanced to the man and knocked his knife out of his hand.

steps.name: Criminal
steps.text: Ahhhhhhh! My hand!

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: My mama died when I was still a kid, but both my fathers told me—

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: If you do bad things, you must answer for your crimes.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Hand over what you stole.

steps.name: Criminal
steps.text: Ugh.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Huh...?

steps.name: Criminal
steps.text: Don't think you're all that just because you've got moves, kid.

steps.name: Criminal
steps.text: This is Dossoles. Lots of groups have their claws in here.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: How do you know this whistle?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: This is a True Bolívarian signal.

steps.name: Criminal
steps.text: Who exactly are you?!

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I am... just a passerby.

steps.name: Criminal
steps.text: Hmph, I don't care who you are, but you'll find out real soon you picked a fight with someone you shouldn't have...

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: I'm pretty sure I told you not to use this signal all the time.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Candela's people have their eyes on us.

steps.name: Criminal
steps.text: Sorry, Boss, I ran into some trouble.

steps.name: Criminal
steps.text: I almost got away, but this punk kid stopped me...

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: From Rhodes Island...?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Tío Tacito.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Rafaela?

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Lower your weapon. She's one of us.

steps.name: Criminal
steps.text: Rafaela... You mean, she's the Colonel's daughter?!

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Why, Tío?

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Come with me, Rafaela. It's a long story.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Give back what you stole.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Will do.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: I thought you went to Rhodes Island with Ernesto. Why are you back?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I took some time off, and I thought I would come home to visit Papá.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Hahaha, I see.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I don't know that man just now.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: He... He's one of my new lackeys. Of course you wouldn't know him.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Tío Tacito, I thought all of you left Dossoles a long time ago.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: A lot of us did leave after the Colonel was arrested... but he's old. Somebody has to take care of him, so a few of us stayed behind.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: You're lying, Tío.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I know you. The Tío I know would chew everyone out just for gambling on cards. You wouldn't let your subordinates do something like this.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: You say the thief's new, but he knows Papá's rank. You're lying. He's not new.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: And this room... It reeks of gunpowder.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: You're trying to put a team together to rescue him, aren't you?

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: You dodged my grapple...? You've improved a lot.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Tío Barrow?!

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: Sorry, Rafaela, but you can't go through here.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: You've gotten a lot smarter. You weren't this observant before.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: At first, I was just going to give you a warm welcome and let you be on your way.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: But you'll need to extend your vacation by a few days, I'm afraid.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: It's okay. I have plenty of paid time off saved up.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I didn't come to stop you guys, either.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: I watched you grow up. If I had a daughter, I would hope she'd be a good girl like you.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: But now I can't let you go before we finish our goal.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Don't blame me for being so ruthless.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: You haven't been on our side ever since you and Ernesto left.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: What are you planning to do?

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: Nothing too different from before. Penetrate, ambush, demolish. Maybe slash Candela's face while we're at it.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: Don't give me that 'isn't there some other way' kind of face like Ernesto, mija.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: Did you know? José is dead.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Barrow!

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: She has a right to know. Am I wrong?

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: But that idiot didn't die in battle. He died because of his gambling.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Candela's a monster. The city she's built is a monster. We're no match for her.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Once we get the Colonel out of there, we're leaving this city.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Let me help.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: But you finally found such a good job. You don't have to get yourself involved.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: All you need to do is to stay here till we're done, and you can go free.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: But I can't just stand by and do nothing.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: Enough, Tacito. How long are you going to keep that up?

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: She's a good girl, but she doesn't listen to anyone.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: She's our daughter! A daughter to every single one of us brothers!

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I'm a Rhodes Islander. They won't be too hard on me. I'll help you make contact with Papá.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: Look at how our daughter's grown.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: We're back.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Look. A fine fowlbeast.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: And I have the spices and other ingredients you wanted.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I cleaned up the kitchen, too. You can just leave the rest to me.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Alright. Us ruffians don't know how to cook. If you need anything, let us know.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Mhm.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: I really need to hand it to you to come up with this roast fowlbeast idea. It's the colonel's favorite.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Fowlbeasts raised for food are usually heftier.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: We could write any messages we want to get to him on paper and stuff them inside, you bring it to the Colonel.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: Maybe we can squeeze some trinkets in there, too.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Yeah, I want Papá to eat something that he likes, even if it's just once in a while.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: He probably hasn't had a good meal inside.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: ...Yeah.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: The Colonel has never been one to indulge in pleasures. He probably hasn't had a very good time in prison.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: He'll be so happy to have a taste of his daughter's roast fowlbeast.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: I'm sure he'll be delighted that you're worried about him. I mean...

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Barrow.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: Fine, I won't bring it up.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Hermano... came back a while ago.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: He paid the colonel a visit and attended a wedding.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: I saw him from a distance. Didn't talk to him.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Do you hate him?

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Hate him? No way.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: If it wasn't for him, all of us would probably have been buried in the wastes, back when the Colonel was arrested.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: He's got a bright future ahead of him. Maybe he'll actually become a successful man one day.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Tío Barrow, hand me that spice.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: You got it.
As the flames grill the fowlbeast meat, a beautiful luster gradually appears.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: Heh, this aroma sure brings me back.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Right... Before we came to Dossoles, we often grilled meat together out in the wilds.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: The kitchen utensils we had don't hold a candle to this stuff, we didn't have all these spices, we had to hunt for meat... It was terrible...

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: But as soon as we got the fire started and everyone started to gather around it, it felt like we could pull through even the harshest hardships.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: So it goes.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: Tacito, catch.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: When did you buy this?

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: Just now.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: How come I didn't notice?

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: Do I even deserve to call myself a scout if you of all people notice me doing anything?

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Hmph.
The bulky soldier doesn't rebuke. Instead, he simply cracks open a can of beer and chugs it.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I want one, too.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: You got it.
La Pluma clumsily pulls the can's tab and holds it with both her hands, drinking its contents in small gulps.
The soldiers never cared much about their beer's quality, and its taste could not be more different from her brew.
But this exciting texture instantly reminds her of how things were before.
There was this one time after Papá won a battle, when everyone celebrated in the camp.
She had already learned how to cook by then, and she loved making food for them.
Hermano preferred quiet places, so he hid in the tent and tried to sleep.

But in the end, with all the noise around him, he had no choice but to come out and try to quiet them down, only for Papá to force him to join them as they drank. Both of them ended up completely hammered.
The camp was filled with cheers and laughter.
Back then, Papá often laughed out loud.
Back then, the things that worried Hermano were written all over his face.
The sizzling of the meat pulls her back to reality.
Suddenly, she is feeling a little thankful for the Doctor.
In the past, she would definitely be hung up on what she should do, and hope that someone would give her an idea.
But now, she knows what to do.

steps.name: Tourist?
steps.text: Ugh.

steps.name: Tourist?
steps.text: It's me.

steps.name: Tourist?
steps.text: Sorry, I lost her, but she's headed toward the prison. She's probably going to make contact with Pancho.

steps.name: Tourist?
steps.text: Yes, she made contact with what's left of Pancho's men.

steps.name: Tourist?
steps.text: Yeah, could very well be connected.

steps.name: Tourist?
steps.text: Assemble the men.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I really wish I could get a compliment from the Doctor at a time like this.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Papá, I'm here.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Oh, mija. You've finally come to visit.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I brought you this, too. It's roast fowlbeast, your favorite.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Hoho, my own daughter's roast fowlbeast. It's been way too long.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Come here and let me get a good look at you.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: You lost weight. Is the food at Rhodes Island that bad?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Not at all. It's very good.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Maybe it's because I've been out on missions a lot lately.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Don't overwork yourself. It's very important to sleep and eat on a regular schedule.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Yeah, I know.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Papá, you have new scars.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Prison is a place where fists do the talking.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: All I did was tell a few men here that just because I'm getting on in years doesn't mean they can pick on me.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I'll bring you some ointment next time.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Alright, alright.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: What do you think of Rhodes Island?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I think... it's a pretty good place. Everyone at the company's very friendly, and they treat us well.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: That's good to hear.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: But you can't settle down if you just keep working for them.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Doesn't Rhodes Island travel to lots of different countries? You should look out when you go to all those different places with them.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: If you find somewhere that works for you, settle down there.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Can't I come back to Bolívar?

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Don't be silly, my daughter.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: There's nothing here in Bolívar. My greatest wish now is for you to live a peaceful life.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: What about Hermano?

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: That malcriado...

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: He's got things he wants to do. Let him do them.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: With the ways things turned out, if he told me he wanted to be Candela's doorman, I'd let him.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: But he never thinks about what exactly it is that he wants to do.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: He's too hesitant and cautious. A man like him can't accomplish anything!

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I... I'm sure he's aware.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: He knows what it is that he wants to do.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: He's just afraid.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Afraid? What could he even be afraid of?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: He's afraid that if he really ended up picking a path, he'd lose you, and he'd lose me.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: ...Is that what you think?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: He doesn't actually talk to me much aboard Rhodes Island.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I think he probably thinks the same way as you do. He wants me to use Rhodes Island to find a place to settle down.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: But... why?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I grew up in Bolívar, too. How come I'm the only one who has to leave this place, and not either of you?

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Because—

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I was part of the rebellion.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I'm not innocent.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: You should never have been involved!

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: But I wasn't willing to just stand by and watch it all happen.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Besides... even if all I did was watch it happen... Does that really clear me of all involvement?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: The more I think about that, the more confused I am—

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: But at the same time, I also understand you and Hermano better and better.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I think I want to do something, too.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I made this roast fowlbeast with Tío Tacito and everyone else.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Tacito...

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: That bastard... Even if the situation is bad, he shouldn't have asked you to do this!

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I wanted to.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I know that things are really complicated.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I'm trying to understand them, but I still don't grasp them completely.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: But there is one thing that I know.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: You can't let the people who respect you and look up to you to die for no reason.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: So... you don't want me to take this fowlbeast. Is that it?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: ...Mhm.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Next time, I'll make you something even tastier.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: This is only the second time you've ever asked something of me.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: You've grown up, Rafaela.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: That's what you all say, but I don't think I'm much different from before.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I just want you to stay healthy and for Hermano to be more careful. It's that simple.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Ernesto came by a while back.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Yeah, I know.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: He asked me if I remember what kind of flower his mother had clipped to her chest the first time we met.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: I told him I don't.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: I really don't.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: That also means... I'm old.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: It was a lilac.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: What? How did you...?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: You told me.
That day, she helped her inebriated father back to the tent, and in his haze, he started to talk.
As he continued, Papá began to cry.
He was remembering his wife.
The flower that she pinned to her chest when he first met her.
A lilac. A beautiful lilac.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Right, it was a lilac.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: How could I forget...?

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Gracias, mija.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Take this fowlbeast back with you.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Are you sure?

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Rafaela, mija.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: There are some things that I thought I'd only say to Ernesto. I never thought I'd have to say any of this to you, too.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Once you've decided to do something, don't be a coward.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: And never let anyone influence your thinking.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: ...alright.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Papá?

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: If you told me what you told Hermano, then... will you tell him the same thing you told me?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Promise me.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: I promise you.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: You ready?

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: Thirty of us. Not one less.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Say, do you think Rafaela will come with?

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: Don't be an idiot.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: Who didn't want to drag her into this before?

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Hah, you're right about that.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Nothing good could come out of following a bunch of men who are doomed to die who-knows-where tomorrow.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: You want to die tomorrow?

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: If you ask me, I think today would do just fine.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Rafaela, you're back.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: How's the Colonel?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: He's the same as he ever was.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: Wait... Why did you bring the fowlbeast back out?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: It's his choice.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Impossible.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: There's no way he's okay with dying in prison.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: You brat... you tricked us.

steps.name: Shrewd Soldier
steps.text: You talked him out of it, didn't you?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Candela's lackeys have been watching you the whole time.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I don't want you to get yourselves killed.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: You've always been so kind, mija.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: But I told you. We don't really have a lot of opportunities left.

steps.name: Bulky Soldier
steps.text: Out of the way.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I won't let you through.
The leader turns to his teammates behind him and nods to signal their impending attack.
This is a hideout of the remnants of Pancho's forces. Intelligence shows that they are planning to break Pancho out of prison.
Her orders are to kill every last one of them.

steps.name: Candela's Subordinate
steps.text: (Quietly) 3, 2, 1—

steps.name: Candela's Subordinate
steps.text: —Huh?
Candela's lackeys find themselves dumbfounded by what they see.
Inside the room, there are only a bunch of groaning soldiers on the ground and a girl standing in the middle.
She is holding a giant scythe. Its blade reflects a cold, awe-inspiring ray of light that lands on her face, revealing two dried up trails of tears.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: What happened?

steps.name: Candela's Subordinate
steps.text: Señora, they've been like this the moment we entered.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: You're Ernesto's...

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I'm an operator from Rhodes Island. Codename La Pluma.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: A Rhodes Island operator... What are you doing here?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I happened across these guerrillas hiding a stash of weapons, so I dealt with them.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: This is a Dossoles matter. You should have notified my subordinates as soon as you found them.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Sorry, Ms. Candela, but it was an emergency.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: I'm sorry myself, that is not enough of a reason.
Before Candela can finish, her subordinates have already leveled their weapons on La Pluma.
Just then—

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: It's me.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: ...Ahah, I see. Very well. I'll be back soon.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: I've had a change of heart, my girl.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: This is a decent enough reason.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Take all of them back. Be good to them.

steps.name: Candela's Subordinate
steps.text: Ms. Candela?

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: An old friend of mine suddenly asked for a chat. I'm in a good mood.

steps.name: Candela's Subordinate
steps.text: Got it.

steps.name: Candela's Subordinate
steps.text: Come! We're picking up all this trash off the floor!

steps.name: Candela's Subordinates
steps.text: Yes, sir!

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: You're a brave one. You won a chance for them to live.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: What's on your mind now?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I'm wondering if I should thank you.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Hahaha.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Ernesto told me about his lovely, well-behaved sister. I didn't pay him any mind at the time, but now it seems his appraisal was biased.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: You know, my child? You should not have done this.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: What you should have done is watch it all happen, and then turn and leave.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: You are still young. You have the right to leave Bolívar.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: What you've done today might have saved a few men, but thanks to this, I will remember you.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: That's not a good thing.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I thought it through, and I decided to do this.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Your brother told me that this country's thorns are what brings him joy.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: What about you? What do you think?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Hermano thought really, really hard about Bolívar.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: At first, I wanted to be like him, but then I found out I can't do that.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I want more people that I can call family, who will stay by my side forever.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Even if you will not be related by blood?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Even though we are not related by blood, I will always be my hermano's sister.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I will always be Papá's daughter.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: If they don't want to leave, then I don't think I should leave, either.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: It's that simple.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: You remind me of back when I took over the city.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: My father was a scumbag. This city is a mess that he left to me to sort out.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: I had the ability to change it, but why should I have?

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Tell me, why?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Because you're your papá's daughter?

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: It's not that simple, but it's also not that complicated.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I don't understand.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: You will, one day.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Now go, mija.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: You are a feather lifted off the ground by a fierce wind. The wind will destroy you without mercy... but if you are tenacious enough, you will see sights that you can see only in the storm.

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: Guapa, you know the store's not going to open. What are you doing spacing out here?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Who are you?

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: I talked to you before. You forgot?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I did.

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: Alright...

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: Here, this is for you.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: Didn't you catch a thief before? The owner wanted to give you a reward, but couldn't find you. So it falls to me.

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: I had no idea where you were, but I figured that if you knew so much about this place, you might come back, so I held onto it for you.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Oh, you're the one who talked to me the other day.

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: That's what I just said!

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: What are you doing here?

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: My flower shop is just nearby.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: A flower shop?

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: Yes, I used to be an athlete. I was in the Championship.

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: One day, I fell in the arena. Just as everyone was booing me on the ground, I saw a flower, like it was smiling at me.

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: So I left the sports world, and opened this shop.

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: Eh, wait!

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: ...Do you have any lilacs?

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: Of course.

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: I want a bundle of them.

steps.name: Flower Shop Owner
steps.text: Are they for someone?

steps.name: La Pluma
steps.text: Si. For my family.
